title: The Book of Judges Timeline
sub: Othniel to Samson · Each Man Did What Was Right in His Own Eyes
desc: A repeating cycle of apostasy, oppression, crying out, and deliverance runs through twelve very different judges — Deborah, Gideon, Jephthah, Samson — spiraling downward into a civil war that nearly erases an entire tribe of Israel.

eras.label: Era One · Judges 1
eras.name: An Incomplete Conquest
eras.dates: After Joshua's death, tribe by tribe, Israel's conquest of Canaan stalls out short of completion, leaving Canaanite enclaves throughout the land

events.title: The Canaanites Managed to Remain in the Land
events.detail: Tribe after tribe fails to fully drive out the Canaanites from its allotted territory, settling instead for forced labor from the peoples they were supposed to remove entirely — a pattern of incomplete obedience that sets up the whole book.

verses.text: “The LORD was with the men of Judah. They conquered the hill country, but they could not conquer the people living in the coastal plain.”

eras.label: Era Two · Judges 2
eras.name: The Cycle of Judges Established
eras.dates: The book's recurring pattern is laid out explicitly: apostasy, oppression, crying out, deliverance, and relapse

events.title: The Israelites Did Evil in the LORD's Sight
events.detail: A new generation that never witnessed the LORD's great deeds abandons him for the Baals, establishing the book's recurring cycle: Israel sins, the LORD hands them to oppressors, they cry out, and he raises up a deliverer — only for the cycle to repeat once that leader dies.

verses.text: “The Israelites did evil before the LORD [Yahweh] by worshiping the Baals.”

eras.label: Era Three · Judges 3
eras.name: Othniel, Ehud, and Shamgar
eras.dates: The first three judges deliver Israel through very different means — a model warrior, a daring left-handed assassin, and an oxgoad

events.title: Othniel's Model Deliverance — Ehud's Hidden Sword — Shamgar's Oxgoad
events.detail: Othniel, Caleb's nephew, delivers Israel from Aram in a deliverance told with model brevity; left-handed Ehud smuggles a hidden sword past an obese Moabite king and assassinates him personally; and Shamgar kills 600 Philistines with nothing but a farming tool.

verses.text: “He killed 600 Philistines with an oxgoad. So he also delivered Israel.”

eras.label: Era Four · Judges 4-5
eras.name: Deborah, Barak, and the Song of Victory
eras.dates: A prophetess leads Israel to victory over a superior chariot army, and a tent peg through the head of a fleeing general becomes the subject of a triumphant victory song

events.title: Jael Drives a Tent Peg Through Sisera's Temple
events.detail: The prophetess Deborah summons Barak to battle against Sisera's 900 iron chariots, warning him he'll gain no personal glory since the LORD will hand the enemy general over to a woman — fulfilled when Jael kills the fleeing Sisera with a tent peg while he sleeps in her tent.

verses.text: “Arise, for this is the day which the LORD [Yahweh] has given Sisera in your hand… has the LORD [Yahweh] not gone out before you?”

events.title: The Song of Deborah — May Your Enemies Perish Like This
events.detail: Deborah and Barak celebrate the victory in one of the oldest pieces of Hebrew poetry in the Bible, praising the tribes who answered the call to battle, shaming those who stayed home, and celebrating Jael as most blessed among women.

verses.text: “May all your enemies perish like this, O LORD [Yahweh]! But may those who love you shine like the rising sun at its brightest.”

eras.label: Era Five · Judges 6
eras.name: Gideon's Call — Tear Down Your Father's Baal Altar
eras.dates: A frightened farmer threshing wheat in hiding is called by the LORD's own angel to become a mighty warrior, and immediately tested at home before he faces any foreign enemy

events.title: The LORD Is With You, O Mighty Warrior — the Fleece Tested Twice
events.detail: Gideon, hiding from Midianite raiders, is called a mighty warrior by the angel of the LORD despite feeling like the least significant man in the weakest clan; after secretly tearing down his own father's Baal altar at night, he twice tests the LORD with a wool fleece before committing to battle.

verses.text: “The angel of the LORD [Yahweh] appeared to him and said, ‘The LORD [Yahweh] is with you, courageous warrior!’”

eras.label: Era Six · Judges 7
eras.name: Gideon's Three Hundred
eras.dates: An army of 32,000 is deliberately whittled down to just 300 men, so no one could claim the coming victory by their own strength

events.title: You Have Too Many Men — Down to Three Hundred
events.detail: The LORD deliberately reduces Gideon's army from 32,000 to just 300 men through two rounds of selection, so Israel could never boast that its own strength won the battle; armed only with trumpets, jars, and torches, the 300 rout the entire Midianite camp.

verses.text: “The LORD [Yahweh] said to Gideon, ‘You have too many men for me to hand Midian over to you. Israel might brag, “Our own strength has delivered us.”’”

eras.label: Era Seven · Judges 8
eras.name: Gideon's Pursuit, Refusal of Kingship, and a Fateful Ephod
eras.dates: Complete victory is followed by a refusal to become king, undercut by a golden ephod that becomes a snare for the very man who refused the crown

events.title: Gideon Captures and Executes the Midianite Kings
events.detail: Gideon completes the rout of Midian, punishing two Israelite towns that refused to help his exhausted army along the way, and personally executes the two captured Midianite kings, Zebah and Zalmunna, who had killed his own brothers.

verses.text: “They were my brothers, the sons of my mother. I swear, as surely as the LORD is alive, if you had let them live, I would not kill you.”

events.title: The LORD Will Rule Over You — Yet an Ephod Becomes a Snare
events.detail: Gideon refuses Israel's offer to make him king, insisting the LORD alone should rule, but then makes a golden ephod from the plunder that becomes an object of worship for all Israel — undermining, in his own lifetime, the very principle he'd just defended.

verses.text: “I will not rule over you, nor will my son rule over you. The LORD will rule over you.”

eras.label: Era Eight · Judges 9
eras.name: Abimelech's Bloody Kingship
eras.dates: Gideon's son murders his own seventy half-brothers to seize power, ruling through violence until a woman with a millstone ends his brief reign

events.title: Abimelech Murders Seventy Brothers — a Millstone Ends His Reign
events.detail: Gideon's son Abimelech murders his seventy half-brothers on one stone to make himself king over Shechem, ruling through bloodshed until a woman drops a millstone on his head during a siege, and he orders his own armor-bearer to finish him off rather than be known as killed by a woman.

verses.text: “God repaid Abimelech for the evil he did to his father by murdering his 70 half brothers.”

eras.label: Era Nine · Judges 10-11
eras.name: Jephthah's Rash Vow
eras.dates: An outcast son becomes Israel's military leader against the Ammonites, and makes a devastating vow he refuses to break even when it costs him his own daughter

events.title: We Have Sinned — the Cycle Repeats Under the Ammonites
events.detail: After Tola and Jair's uneventful leadership, Israel again turns to foreign gods and suffers under Ammonite and Philistine oppression, finally throwing away their idols and genuinely crying out to the LORD, who grows weary of watching Israel suffer.

verses.text: “They threw away the foreign gods they owned and worshiped the LORD. Finally the LORD grew tired of seeing Israel suffer so much.”

events.title: Jephthah's Vow — His Daughter Meets Him at the Door
events.detail: Jephthah, an outcast son of a prostitute, is recalled to lead Gilead against the Ammonites and makes a rash vow to sacrifice whatever comes through his door first if granted victory — tragically, it is his only daughter who comes out to greet him.

verses.text: “Jephthah made a vow to the LORD [Yahweh], saying, ‘If you really do hand the Ammonites over to me.’”

eras.label: Era Ten · Judges 12
eras.name: Shibboleth — the Minor Judges
eras.dates: A civil war within Israel itself is settled by a single mispronounced word, followed by a brief roll call of minor judges

events.title: Say 'Shibboleth' — 42,000 Ephraimites Fall
events.detail: Furious at being excluded from the Ammonite campaign, Ephraim goes to war against Jephthah's Gilead, and the Gileadites identify fleeing Ephraimites by their inability to pronounce 'Shibboleth' correctly, executing 42,000 at the Jordan's fords before three minor judges briefly lead Israel.

verses.text: “If he said, ‘Sibboleth’ (and could not pronounce the word correctly), they grabbed him and executed him right there at the fords of the Jordan.”

eras.label: Era Eleven · Judges 13
eras.name: The Birth of Samson
eras.dates: An angel announces the birth of a Nazirite deliverer to a childless couple, in a scene that ends with the couple realizing they've been speaking with the divine

events.title: The Angel of the LORD Announces Samson's Birth
events.detail: An angel appears to a childless woman promising a son dedicated to God as a Nazirite from birth; when the angel ascends in the flame of their offering, Manoah and his wife realize they've encountered the LORD's own messenger face to face.

verses.text: “The angel of the LORD [Yahweh] appeared to the woman and said to her, ‘You are infertile and childless, but you will conceive and have a son.’”

eras.label: Era Twelve · Judges 14-15
eras.name: Samson's Riddle and Revenge
eras.dates: A doomed marriage to a Philistine woman becomes the pretext for a personal vendetta, escalating from a wedding riddle to a jawbone massacre

events.title: Out of the Strong Came Something Sweet — the Riddle Betrayed
events.detail: Samson's insistence on marrying a Philistine woman turns out to be the LORD's own means of stirring up conflict with Israel's oppressors; his wedding riddle about honey in a lion's carcass is betrayed to the guests by his own bride under pressure.

verses.text: “His father and mother did not realize this was the LORD's doing because he was looking for an opportunity to stir up trouble with the Philistines.”

events.title: A Thousand Men With the Jawbone of a Donkey
events.detail: Escalating revenge cycles between Samson and the Philistines climax in his single-handed slaughter of a thousand men with nothing but a donkey's jawbone, after which he cries out to the LORD for water and is miraculously revived at the point of death.

verses.text: “With the jawbone of a donkey I have left them in heaps; with the jawbone of a donkey I have struck down a thousand men!”

eras.label: Era Thirteen · Judges 16
eras.name: Samson and Delilah
eras.dates: The strongman's fatal weakness for a Philistine woman leads to betrayal, blindness, and a final act of devastating, self-sacrificial vengeance

events.title: Delilah's Betrayal — Let Me Die With the Philistines
events.detail: Delilah wears Samson down until he reveals the secret of his Nazirite vow, and his shaved hair costs him his strength, his eyes, and his freedom — until, blinded and mocked in the Philistine temple of Dagon, his hair regrown, he pulls down the pillars in one final act that kills more enemies in his death than in his life.

verses.text: “Samson called to the LORD, ‘O Sovereign LORD [Adonai Yahweh], remember me! Strengthen me just one more time, O God [Elohim].’”

eras.label: Era Fourteen · Judges 17-18
eras.name: Micah's Idols and the Danite Migration
eras.dates: Without any king to enforce true worship, a private household shrine becomes the seed of an entire tribe's idolatry

events.title: Each Man Did What Was Right in His Own Eyes — Micah's Private Shrine
events.detail: Micah dedicates stolen silver to make idols for a private household shrine, hiring a wandering Levite as his personal priest and mistakenly believing this arrangement guarantees the LORD's blessing — a snapshot of religious confusion in a nation without a king.

verses.text: “In those days Israel had no king. Each man did what he considered to be right.”

events.title: The Tribe of Dan Steals Micah's Idols and His Priest
events.detail: The migrating tribe of Dan, searching for territory, steals Micah's idols and hires away his priest to establish their own corrupt worship center, permanently institutionalizing the idolatry that began in one man's private household.

verses.text: “You stole my gods that I made, as well as this priest, and then went away. What do I have left?”

eras.label: Era Fifteen · Judges 19-21
eras.name: The Levite's Concubine and Civil War Against Benjamin
eras.dates: The book's darkest chapter, a horrific crime in Gibeah, spirals into a devastating civil war that nearly erases an entire Israelite tribe

events.title: A Horrific Crime at Gibeah
events.detail: A Levite's concubine is brutally abused and killed by men of Gibeah in Benjamin's territory, and the Levite dismembers her body and sends the pieces throughout Israel's tribes as a shocking call to collective action — the moral low point of the entire book.

verses.text: “Nothing like this has happened or been witnessed during the entire time since the Israelites left the land of Egypt!”

events.title: Civil War — Israel Nearly Annihilates the Tribe of Benjamin
events.detail: When Benjamin refuses to hand over the guilty men of Gibeah, the rest of Israel wages a brutal civil war that all but wipes out the tribe of Benjamin, reducing it to just 600 surviving men.

verses.text: “The LORD annihilated Benjamin before Israel; the Israelites struck down that day 25,100 sword-wielding Benjaminites.”

events.title: Every Man Did What Was Right in His Own Eyes
events.detail: Regretting their near-annihilation of a whole tribe, Israel devises two morally troubling schemes to find wives for Benjamin's survivors, and the book closes with its haunting refrain that in the absence of a king, every man simply did what seemed right in his own eyes.

verses.text: “In those days Israel had no king. Each man did what he considered to be right in his own eyes.”
